paragraphs: A Mercedes-Benz OM654 engine rebuild starts from £3,600, regardless of which of the six models it's fitted to — the price tier is set by the engine, not the badge on the boot. A full replacement engine and fitting service is also available.
Exact pricing depends on the condition of your existing engine and the parts required — submit your registration for a fixed-price quote within 30 minutes.

cards.title: Rebuilding Your
cards.body: Most engine suppliers sell you a used engine of unknown history and hope it matches. We rebuild the engine your Mercedes already has instead — strip it down, pressure-test it, and replace every worn or damaged component with updated OEM parts. You get a near-new engine with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty, without the compatibility risk of an unknown used unit. This is the option most OM654 owners choose.

cards.title: Replacement
cards.body: If your existing engine is beyond economical repair, we also offer full engine replacement and fitting — sourced and fitted by our team, with the same 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

cards.title: Used
cards.body: In some cases, a matched low-mileage used engine is the right call — particularly if you need your car back on the road quickly and your existing engine's damage is extensive. We can source and fit these too, though most owners who ask about used engines end up choosing a rebuild once they understand the compatibility risk a used unit carries.

options.body: "Reconditioned" is the term many owners search for when they mean the same thing as a rebuild — a full strip-down, inspection, and replacement of worn parts rather than a straight swap. If that's what you're after, our rebuild service is exactly that.
"Refurbished" often describes the same process from a different angle — restoring your existing engine to full working condition rather than replacing it outright. Our rebuild covers this.

Some owners specifically search for a "remanufactured" engine, expecting a unit rebuilt to original specification with updated components. That's consistent with what our rebuild service delivers, regardless of which of the six OM654-equipped models you drive.

faqLeft.q: What is the Mercedes-Benz OM654 engine?
faqLeft.a: The OM654 is Mercedes-Benz's second-generation modular 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel engine, in production since 2016. It's all-aluminium construction with 2,700 bar injection pressure.

faqLeft.q: Which Mercedes-Benz models use the OM654?
faqLeft.a: A-Class, C-Class, E-Class, GLC-Class, GLE-Class, Sprinter, V-Class and Vito — see the full applications table above for exact variants and years.

faqLeft.q: Does the OM654 differ between Mercedes-Benz models?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The specific ancillaries, mounting, and 48V MHEV integration differ by application, even though the base engine code is the same. We match by registration/VIN before confirming any rebuild or replacement.

faqLeft.q: Is an OM654 from one Mercedes-Benz model compatible with another?
faqLeft.a: Not automatically. An OM654 from an A-Class isn't a drop-in match for an OM654 from a Sprinter — ancillaries, mounting, and exhaust/SCR systems all differ. We always confirm compatibility by registration/VIN.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes-Benz OM654 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £2,200, regardless of which model it's fitted to. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.
Yes. We work on OM654 rebuilds across every model it's fitted to, replacing worn components as standard.

faqLeft.q: Do you work on OM654 MHEV (48V) applications?
faqLeft.a: Yes. OM654 48V mild-hybrid applications are within our workshop capability, with the relevant hybrid ancillaries accounted for once your exact model is confirmed.

faqLeft.q: Can you rebuild an OM654 from an E-Class?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The OM654 in the E-Class is one of the most common applications we see, across both the W213 and W214 generations.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an OM654 from a Sprinter?
faqRight.a: Yes. The OM654 in the Sprinter is one of the commercial vehicle applications we work on regularly.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Mercedes-Benz OM654 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Mercedes-Benz if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an OM654 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your vehicle arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most OM654 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history — a particular concern given how many different OM654 applications exist across the Mercedes-Benz range — and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

faqRight.q: Is the OM654 the same as the OM651?
faqRight.a: No. The OM654 is Mercedes-Benz's second-generation modular four-cylinder diesel, replacing the OM651 from 2016 onward. It's an all-aluminium design (17% lighter) with a rear-mounted timing chain and 2,700 bar injection pressure.

faqRight.q: Does the OM654 have timing chain issues?
faqRight.a: The OM654's timing chain is rear-mounted, which means access requires gearbox removal. Early production units showed some timing chain-related issues, but we inspect the chain as standard on every rebuild rather than assuming a specific failure pattern.

faqRight.q: Are 2016-2018 OM654 engines different from later units?
faqRight.a: Some early production OM654 units (2016-2018) showed premature rocker arm/camshaft wear at 100,000-120,000 km, and some injector issues on early builds. Later units appear more robust, but we treat every OM654 on its own condition.
